newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil- Prices soared $6.00 on strong bids.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil- Prices soared $6.00 on strong bids.

text.p: The high sulphur fuel oil market soared by $6.00 per tonne on the back of strong swaps, firm bids amid steady crude prices, traders said on Tuesday.
A major sold 20,000 tonnes of 180-cst grade to a local trading company at $104.5 per tonne for lifting between March 30 and April 3, up from $98 on Monday, traders said.
Fuel oil swaps soared from Monday with aggressive bids from local buyers, traders said.
March and April swaps jumped to $101.75/$102.75 and $99.50/$100.75 respectively, compared with Monday's $98.00 and $96.25.
"We are quite balanced on the supply side now...prices should not go up that much," said one trader, noting that a local trader has been pushing up prices since late Monday.
"It's hard to tell if it's only the trader is pricing up or it's an indication that Chinese players are coming back soon," the trader said.
Demand has been poor from China before the Lunar New Year in early February and traders said China had covered most of its requirements for the first half of March.
Several traders said they saw few fresh enquiries from China for end-March or early-April cargoes but most Chinese players remained inactive.
One trader said Chinese players bid at very low prices.
The bunker market also strengthened on the back of firm swaps. Suppliers, unwilling to sell, are waiting for prices to move higher in the near term, traders said.
Scheduled refinery maintenance turnarounds at Mobil and Singapore Refining Co in Singapore have also boosted sentiment and strengthened prices, they said.
